processMetrics.note: Host process sampling and memory-size queries were denied; no GPU utilization metric was available.

hypotheses: H1: browser main-thread scheduling saturation under concurrent page workloads
H2: headless software-WebGL rendering combined with multiple active renderer pages
H3: test-specific UI actionability or layout defects independent of contention
H4: renderer/GPU context loss or stale RTT work
H5: Vite server or browser process infrastructure contention
experimentDesign.repetitions: One captured independent run per listed matrix point; bounded diagnostic comparisons; no retry loop.
experimentDesign.stoppingRule: Stop after identifying repeatable worker sensitivity, collecting non-invasive bounded probes, and running light-page versus renderer-page and headed controls.

instrumentation.method: Temporary test-only helper recorded 1-second timer heartbeats, bounded requestAnimationFrame intervals, PerformanceObserver long tasks, document visibility, existing renderer DOM attributes, RTT request/completion IDs, and context-loss events.
instrumentation.sourceNote: The helper was temporarily applied in an uncommitted test-only patch atop the accepted base for diagnostic runs, then removed before the scheduling candidate commit. Diagnostic raw report artifacts contain the probe attachments.

sharedCause.commonFactor: Headless Chromium selected ANGLE SwiftShader software WebGL; concurrent renderer-heavy pages coincided with severe long-task totals and large timer/rAF gaps. A live renderer companion reproduced J2 timeout in headless mode; a blank companion did not, and the same renderer companion in headed Metal mode passed quickly.
notEstablished: one verified causal mechanism common to all three tests
